description: Reasoning vault aligned with OpenStax Algebra and Trigonometry 2e §3.7: verify inverse pairs, find inverse formulas, swap domain and range, restrict domains to make functions one-to-one, and interpret inverse graphs.

archetypes.name: Verify an Inverse Pair
archetypes.source: OpenStax Algebra and Trigonometry 2e §3.7 — Verifying Inverse Functions
archetypes.coreConcept: Two functions are inverses when each composition undoes the other on the appropriate domains.
archetypes.mentalModel: Run one function and then the other in both orders; a genuine reversible pair returns each admissible input unchanged.

cognitiveTraps.description: Checking only one composition and assuming the reverse composition also works.
Treating the inverse function as the reciprocal of the output.
Changing the sign incorrectly when moving a constant while solving for the inverse.

archetypes.figureNone: This archetype verifies symbolic compositions; algebraic cancellation directly establishes whether both functions undo each other.

archetypes.name: Find an Inverse Formula
archetypes.source: OpenStax Algebra and Trigonometry 2e §3.7 — Finding the Inverse of a Function
archetypes.coreConcept: Solve y=f(x) for x in terms of y, then exchange the variable labels to express the inverse output as a function of its input.
archetypes.mentalModel: Reverse the input-output roles, solve for the old input, and rename the old output as the new input.

cognitiveTraps.description: Exchanging x and y but failing to isolate the inverse output.
Interpreting the superscript -1 as a reciprocal instead of an inverse function.
Changing the sign incorrectly when moving a constant while solving for the inverse.
Adding the constant instead of subtracting it when evaluating a linear inverse.

archetypes.figureNone: The requested result is an algebraic formula; symbolic isolation is the direct method.

archetypes.name: Restrict a Domain and Swap Domain with Range
archetypes.source: OpenStax Algebra and Trigonometry 2e §3.7 — Domain and Range of an Inverse Function; Restricting the Domain
archetypes.coreConcept: A function must be one-to-one on its domain to have an inverse function; an appropriate restriction can remove repeated outputs, and inverse domain and range exchange roles.
archetypes.mentalModel: Choose one branch so every output identifies exactly one input, then reverse all input-output pairs and their sets.

cognitiveTraps.description: Choosing a restriction that still leaves repeated outputs or conflicts with the requested branch.
Keeping the original domain and range in the same roles for the inverse.

archetypes.name: Interpret Inverse Graphs and Coordinates
archetypes.source: OpenStax Algebra and Trigonometry 2e §3.7 — Graphing an Inverse Function
archetypes.coreConcept: Inverse functions exchange ordered-pair coordinates, so their graphs reflect across y=x.
archetypes.mentalModel: Swap each point's horizontal and vertical coordinates; the mirror line is the diagonal y=x.

cognitiveTraps.description: Reflecting across a coordinate axis instead of the line y=x.
Changing a point without exchanging its input and output coordinates.
